Ziba
ZYE-buh
proper noun
From the Hebrew, perhaps meaning “plant” or “a statue.”

Biblical Definition

Ziba was a servant of the house of Saul, a man with fifteen sons and twenty servants of his own. When David sought to show the kindness of God to any that remained of Saul’s house for Jonathan’s sake, Ziba was summoned and disclosed that Jonathan had a son yet living, Mephibosheth, lame in his feet. David restored to Mephibosheth all the land of Saul and appointed Ziba and his household to till it, that the king’s table might feed his master’s son. Thus far Ziba served faithfully. But when Absalom’s rebellion drove David from Jerusalem, Ziba met the fleeing king with asses laden and provision—and with a slander. He charged that Mephibosheth had stayed behind hoping to seize the kingdom of his fathers, and David, in haste, granted Ziba all that was Mephibosheth’s. Yet when David returned in peace, Mephibosheth came mourning, unwashed and unkempt since the king departed, and protested that Ziba had deceived him, leaving him no beast to ride. David, unable to sift the matter, divided the land between them; and Mephibosheth, in love for the king, said, Let him take all. Ziba stands as a portrait of the opportunist—a servant who served while it profited him, then bore false witness to advance himself in a day of his master’s distress.

Webster 1828 Definition

A servant of Saul’s house who served Mephibosheth, then slandered him to David to seize his inheritance.

expand to see more

ZIBA, a servant of the house of Saul, having fifteen sons and twenty servants.

He revealed to David that Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth was yet living and lame (2Sa 9:3).

He was appointed to till Saul’s restored land for Mephibosheth’s sake.

In Absalom’s revolt he met fleeing David with gifts and slandered his master (2Sa 16:3).

David first gave him all Mephibosheth’s land, then divided it between them (2Sa 19:29).

Key Scripture

2Sa 9:3 — "And the king said, Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may shew the kindness of God unto him? And Ziba said unto the king, Jonathan hath yet a son, which is lame on his feet."

2Sa 16:3 — "And the king said, And where is thy master’s son? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he abideth at Jerusalem: for he said, To day shall the house of Israel restore me the kingdom of my father."

2Sa 16:4 — "Then said the king to Ziba, Behold, thine are all that pertained unto Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I humbly beseech thee that I may find grace in thy sight, my lord, O king."

2Sa 19:29 — "And the king said unto him, Why speakest thou any more of thy matters? I have said, Thou and Ziba divide the land."

Modern Corruption

Ziba is the type of the self-serving slanderer who exploits a master’s extremity for his own gain.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The lesson to recover is the wickedness of bearing false witness against a defenceless man for profit. Ziba served Mephibosheth so long as the service paid; but in David’s day of flight he saw advantage and slandered the lame son of Jonathan, snatching at an inheritance that was not his. The eighth and ninth commandments alike are trodden under his ambition.

Ziba’s opportunism is set in sharp relief against Mephibosheth’s devotion, who cared nothing for the land so long as the king came home in peace. The contrast warns the believer: love that clings to the master is precious in God’s sight, while the calculating heart that profits by another’s ruin is loathsome, though it bring gifts in its hands.

Hebrew Roots

The name is obscure, fitting a man known less for himself than for his treachery toward his master’s son.

expand to see more

Ziba — Hebrew Tsiva, of uncertain sense, perhaps “plant” or “statue.”

He is identified solely as a servant of the house of Saul.

His large household of sons and servants marks him a man of substance.

His name is linked always with Mephibosheth, whom he served and betrayed.

Scripture leaves the final verdict to the divided land and the king’s weary word.

Usage

"Like Ziba, the false servant gives gifts with one hand and slanders with the other."

"Ziba met the fleeing king with provision, but his heart sought another’s inheritance."

"Beware the Ziba who serves only while the serving profits him."
